extracted.intended_audience: Undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD students in the humanities/social sciences pursuing German Studies at US or Canadian universities (and their faculty nominators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/submission requirements for applying to the DAAD German Studies Research Grant (short-term, 1–2 month research stays in Germany) including who may be nominated, required materials, formatting, deadlines, and usage restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduates with at least junior (third-year) standing pursuing a German Studies track or minor may be nominated for the grant by the professor supervising their research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nomination by the supervising professor is required. Undergraduates must meet standing and program/course requirements (see language and coursework requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Master’s-level graduate student eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Master’s level graduate students in the humanities and social sciences earning a certificate or working on a project in German Studies may be nominated for the grant by the professor supervising their research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be nominated by the supervising professor and meet language/course requirements; provide official transcripts of undergraduate and graduate work completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD student eligibility and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD students in the humanities and social science disciplines preparing their dissertation proposals on modern German topics may be nominated by their principal advisor. Students whose dissertation proposals have already been formally accepted one year or more before the application deadline are not eligible for nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is short-term exploratory research to determine viability or delimit scope of proposed dissertations. Program is not intended to supplement or substitute for regular dissertation field work abroad, which should lag the short-term research stay by at least one semester. Advanced doctoral students are advised to consider DAAD’s Research Grants instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and German Studies coursework requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants are expected to have completed two years of college-level German language studies and a minimum of three courses in German Studies (literature, history, politics or other fields) at the time of nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should list German language and German Studies courses taken as part of the application package; the DAAD language evaluation form is also mandatory (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship, enrollment and residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the US and Canada who are enrolled full-time at the US or Canadian college or university that nominates them, or, in the case of international students, must be enrolled in a degree program at a US or Canadian college or university and living in the US or Canada for a minimum of six months by the time of the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify full-time enrollment at the nominating institution and, for international students, evidence of six months residence in US/Canada by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination by faculty supervisor/advisor required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be nominated by the professor supervising their research project (undergraduates and Master’s students) or by their principal advisor (PhD students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations come from faculty; one of the two required recommendation letters must be from the supervising professor. Follow institutional procedures for nomination and ensure faculty submit recommendation materials as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose, duration and ineligible contexts for the award
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant may be used for short-term research (one to two months) in Germany and is designed to encourage interdisciplinary research and promote study of cultural, political, historical, economic and social aspects of modern and contemporary German affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support cannot be provided for stays in Germany in the context of study abroad programs. The program is intended for short-term exploratory work rather than ongoing dissertation fieldwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Research support ranging in value from $2,000 to $3,000 is available to individual scholarship recipients and is intended to offset living and travel costs during the active research phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any awards made will be subject to the ratification of the German federal budget for the same fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and postmark policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Deadlines: May 1 and November 1. Applications postmarked the day of the deadline or earlier will be accepted; those with later postmarks cannot be processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application deadlines for 2026 are May 1 and November 1. Meet the postmark cutoff—late-postmarked applications are invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete applications invalid; materials not returned; no reasons given
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete applications are invalid. Please note: Application materials will not be returned, and no reasons for a decision will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every required component is included; keep copies, as submitted materials will not be returned and DAAD will not provide reasons for selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application format and physical presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible all parts of the application form should be electronically generated, typewritten, or otherwise neatly printed. Please do not staple any of the application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neat, legible presentation is required. Avoid staples and ensure printed materials are clean and professional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential letters of recommendation and official transcripts handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential letters of recommendation and official transcripts should be forwarded in sealed envelopes. Two letters of recommendation are required, including one from the professor supervising the German Studies research project or curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders are asked to send a scan of the signed letter to the provided grandel@daad.de email address; nonetheless, original confidential letters/transcripts should be provided in sealed envelopes as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAAD language evaluation form (Sprachzeugnis) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD language evaluation form (“Sprachzeugnis”) is a mandatory part of the application form, and must be completed and signed by a faculty member of the German Department at the applicant’s institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the completed, signed Sprachzeugnis with the application. This is mandatory and omission will render the application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components (complete package)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application consists of: Completed DAAD application form; Curriculum vitae (résumé); Detailed description of the research project or the pre-dissertation proposal, including a research plan, timeline, and itinerary with specific start and end dates; Budget statement; List of German language and German Studies courses taken; Two letters of recommendation (one from supervising professor); DAAD language evaluation form; Official transcripts (Master’s/PhD: all undergraduate and graduate work; Undergraduates: all undergraduate work completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optionally, applicants may include a host invitation letter from a contact/advisor in Germany to strengthen the application; it is not required and omission will not be held against the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method: paper and electronic versions required
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be handed in 1) via regular mail (see address) and 2) via email to grandel@daad.de in a single pdf-file. In order for your application to be complete, you must hand in an electronic and a paper version of your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the paper packet to the specified DAAD New York address AND email a single PDF of the entire application to the email given. Both are required for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD will announce its decision approximately eight weeks after each deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan travel and other arrangements accordingly; awards are not final until announced and subject to budget ratification.
